searchText: > all we need is a directory with keystore files and then we can import them into Prysm 🙂 <@!387720149345763329> Same deal for Lighthouse <@387720149345763329>, Nimbus's workflow is very similar as well. All you have to do is: ``` beacon_node deposits import <some-directory> ``` it will scan the sub-directories recursively for keystore files and it will import them in our own database. If the keystores are password-protected, you'll be asked to provide the password interactively Teku just needs you to give us the path to your keystores and we'll read them from there. No import necessary. > Hi <@!387720149345763329> you should be able to import keystore files created in lighthouse, what errors do you get if you use the prysm.sh validator accounts-v2 import command ? <@!311971895828283393> not working. message: **Importing accounts, this may take a while... Please try again, could not use password to import account 0x9092dff7283b:** plain text password was provided, however, looks like lighthouse does not use that plaintext directly, instead, it uses encrypted plaintext -- it encrypt the plaintext password first, then save it to a file under secrects folder, then use that file to decrypt keystore. launchpad use straight plaintext password when i input the encrypted password, such as *nONOQvpPuQ07xn3dUawmVOc0lxcvQ3xvBFiTYm5LbstfPlZu*, error: **Incorrect password entered, please try again** Also, although a batch use same pass-phase, each keysore has a different encrypted password file generated. <@!361447803194441738> <@!311971895828283393> i'm using lighthouse to batch generate keystores and do batch deposit. I used to do the same thing via prysm. unfortunately, prysm's batch-deposit script has not yet upgrade to Medalla.

excerpts.author: zahary.
excerpts.content:
<@387720149345763329>, Nimbus's workflow is very similar as well. All you have to do is:

```
beacon_node deposits import <some-directory>
```

it will scan the sub-directories recursively for keystore files and it will import them in our own database. If the keystores are password-protected, you'll be asked to provide the password interactively

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Teku just needs you to give us the path to your keystores and we'll read them from there.  No import necessary.
